problem:
Title: Characterization of Pointwise Maximum of Real-Valued Functions

Let $S$ be a [[Definition:Set|set]].

Let $\R$ denote the [[Definition:Real Number Line|real number line]].

Let $f, g :S \to \R$ be [[Definition:Real-Valued Function|real-valued functions]].

Let $f \vee g$ denote the [[Definition:Pointwise Maximum of Real-Valued Functions|pointwise maximum]] of $f$ and $g$, that is, $f \vee g$ is the [[Definition:Mapping|mapping]] defined by:
:$\forall s \in S : \map {\paren{f \vee g} } s = \max \set{\map f s, \map g s}$

Then:
:$f \vee g = \dfrac 1 2 \paren{f + g + \size{f - g}}$
where:
:$f + g$ denotes the [[Definition:Pointwise Addition of Real-Valued Functions|pointwise addition]] of $f$ and $g$
:$f - g$ denotes the [[Definition:Pointwise Difference of Real-Valued Functions|pointwise difference]] of $f$ and $g$
:$\size{f - g}$ denotes the [[Definition:Absolute Value of Real-Valued Function|absolute value]] of $f - g$
:$\dfrac 1 2 \paren{f + g + \size{f - g}}$ denotes the [[Definition:Pointwise Scalar Multiplication of Real-Valued Function|pointwise scalar multiplication]] of $f + g + \size{f - g}$ by $\dfrac 1 2$
